Love in Lockdown

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Three totally different love stories with one thing in common they all happened during lockdown

Further information:
Our phone affair
He dropped her a DM on FB, they started chatting and then the president announced lockdown. So for the next 7 weeks they spoke on the phone every day. For hours they got to know each other, watched tv together, cooked meals together and had coffee dates all over video chat. “I don’t know if we would have spent so much time getting to know each other if it wasn’t for lockdown. I am always busy and have worked hard at avoiding these intimate situations for a while” but with lockdown Nokuzola had nowhere to run, so she let him in and last week they went on their first real life date. They social distanced and wore masks, but the spark was there in person as much as it has been over the phone.
Visually:
We can do this piece super stylistically
We can re-enact their lockdown love life over the phone.
Then go on a socially distancing date with them

Married in lockdown
This one is a winner, Dan Mace is a filmmaker in CT. He then got COVID in the USA where he isolated for 14 days. He then came home and the president announced SA’s lockdown
Him and his fiancé had to call off their wedding because of the lockdown
But after a few weeks in lockdown he realised he wanted to be married more than he wanted a wedding. So he stayed awake all night creating cardboard cut-outs as guests and set up a wedding in isolation. The wedding was officiated by a minister on skype and the ipad was stuck to the head of a cardboard cut-out. Dan has amazing visuals of the whole wedding.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?time_continue=2&v=jITaE9ib6Fs&feature=emb_logo
Visually
Dan is willing to allow us to use the documentation of the wedding and their relationship, as long as we credit him

This one is from the original proposal
She got divorced before her 32 birthday to the man she thought she would love forever. They had a yoga studio and were set to open a vegan restaurant. It took years to find her feet again and then she met a guy 6 years younger than her. They are both super spiritual hippy types who love Africa Burn. Lockdown made them see what really mattered in life and just before it lifted they got engaged. “I want to give you my heart until the end” Michelle posted on their Engagement post

Script:


00:00 – 00:36
VO: COVID-19 has changed everything as we know it. Our masks hide our smiles. People are isolated and alone at a time when we need each other more than ever. But these three love stories will inspire all of us to find a way to spread the love

Dan: the whole world is experiencing the same pain the same suffering in two different respects really does bring home what's important
upsound: Miss you I love you
Dan up sound about the starts aligning with Gabi at Fat cactus

00:37 – 2:01
When fate took Dan Mace a filmmaker and international youtube sensation to a Mexican restaurant one night, he never expected to lock eyes with the love of his life

Dan
we were doing our wrap party and I saw this girl in the distance. This beautiful brunette.
And I've never done this before and it sounds like something my dad would do, like a pickup line. But I said to the waitress you see those two girls over there. Can you bring them two shots.
Mas: like in the movies?
Gabs: exactly like the movies
And then Gabs turned around. And looked at me and was like Dan And I was like Shit I'm getting famous this person knows who I am. And then when she got closer I obviously realized it was Gabby

Upsound from Dan youtube video: Gabi is Dans besties sister

Mace works between the USA and South Africa. In March this year he returned to Cape-Town to marry the girl of his dreams

Dan: I flew back a week before the wedding
I mean everything was planned Perfectly for us
Dan: you
Gab: for me.
Dan I'm joking…
When I was coming back from my Bachelor's not Sunday Cyril addressed the nation to gatherings for less than 100 people were illegal
so that monday we had decided to cancel the wedding …
Gaby: postponed
Dn: I always say cancel which is like I guess postpone.

2:01 – 4:07
Bertram Malgas and Monique Mortlock met in 2014 and 2020 was supposed to be the year they took their love to the next level, but then lockdown happened

Monique: we actually meet each other at a OR Tambo International Airport . I had struggled to get my suitcase off of the carousel then this Handsomeish guy he just jumped in and he jumped in and he was like ah let me me get it for you.

Since that day at OR Tambo Monique and Bertram have spent the past 6 years living out a fairytale love story.

Upsound

Until the pandemic hit South Africa. They are both journalists reporting from the frontline of COVID-19, which is a job that comes with high risks

Bert: we go into communities that are hot spots and we interacting with a lot of people and it's a virus that we can't see. So we have to take the precautions

Bertrams parents have multiple comorbidities making them vulnerable to the virus. SO these two that use to be inseparable have made a pact not to see each other until its safe again

Bert : Ya so I haven’t seen Monique since lockdown started
mon: I am not coping as well as he is. He can tell you your many many days when I tell him lets just meet secretly no one will know I Just want to kiss you.

mas: So how are you to Bertram keeping your relationship alive during lockdown.
Mon: everything we are doing is on the phone. just having fake little date night chats on video call and just speaking to each other and when I'm watching a movie he'll maybe watch it as well. And then we can either laugh about what makes the movie terrible
Mas: so it's almost like watching it together.
MON: and there'd be nights WHEN I'm falling asleep and HE would still be watching me and chatting to me. And it's quite soothing actually.

4:07 - 5:33
Michell in Malawi upsound

Michelle and Dan are travel obsessed, adventure seeking 30 somethings. Who met at work, became besties and fell madly in love. They were living their dream life until they were in lockdown in their flat together for months

Mas: How would you describe your relationship. What kind of love do you share.
dan: I think wanting the best for the other person. I think that's like a core thing. And then on top of that is seeking adventure living in the moment
mish: something both of us realized when we got together was just how much we really wanted to do life together. And like not hold back.
Mish: We kind of we went from an adventurous kind of travel a lot with a lot of external escape to really kind of Looking within and looking to one another and really looking at what we wanted together as a future.






5:33 – 6:52
So while COVID-19 is putting everybody else’s love plans on hold. Mace was determined to find a way to give Gabi a version of her dream wedding
Upsound from Dan
and made this youtube video of the whole experience
Upsound from Dan
Dan: So this was peak lockdown
Mas: what level of lock down?
DAN: You can't even leave your house like lockdown.
Dan: This is before the levels.
Mas: oh the original lock down
Dan: So I had to make use of everything I had

Upsound from the youtube video

Dan I made the walkway out of leftover bricks from the renovations we were doing. And I cut out a priest so that I could put my friend Jonah on Zoom

Upsound from youtube video

6:54 – 7:24
From Lockdown weddings to engagements. If Michelle and Dan imagined their engagement story it definitely wouldn’t start with them sitting on a couch

We did this meditation on the couch one evening. And yeah we opened our eyes and afterwards Dan looked at me and he was like Will you marry me and I was kind of like woah
Dan: you were like are we having a conversation. Are you asking the thing.
Mish: So we just had to confirm that that was the question. And yeah it was.
dan: I found the person I want to spend the rest of my life with. Honestly it was it was so simple.

7:25 – 8:04
While COVID- 19 brought Michelle and Dan closer, it has forced Bertram and Monique to press pause on their 2020 plans

at the start of 2020 I thought This is the year we going to get married
I had all of these ideas and all of these dreams and then the lockdown happened
Just seeing with the rest of the world was going. I knew it wasn't just going to be a month. It wasn't just going to be two months. We were probably going to be in this for the long haul. So I kind of resigned myself to putting some of those ideas on ice. It wasn't easy especially for me
mon: there have Been many nights I have cried

8:05 – 9:00
Sometimes when the world seems completely upside down, the sadness is overwhelming and tomorrow is a constant uncertainty we just need hold to onto the love

Dans Youtube video upsound

Dan: you looked beautiful walking down the isle and I was like oh my god am I going to cry
all in all it was like the most beautiful imperfect and impromptu experience of.

Even though it feels like COVID-19 is not going anywhere, there will be a day when we will be free again and making plans for when that happens is giving these couple hope

Mas: What would you say this pandemic has taught you both about love
Gab: that it's real actually. That it actually really exists
